q1.pergunta: How much money do I actually need to buy a home in BC?
q1.resposta: More than the down payment. You also need closing costs, Property Transfer Tax, inspection, lawyer or notary fees and, in a strata, the monthly fees from day one. The exact number depends on the price range and the type of property, and we go through it together before you start looking. The free guide gives you the full list.

q2.pergunta: Is this a good time to buy or sell?
q2.resposta: It depends far more on your situation than on the headlines. Your financing, your timeline, how long you plan to stay and what is available in your range matter more than the general market number. That is exactly what the first conversation is for.

q3.pergunta: Do I pay anything to work with you as a buyer?
q3.resposta: In a typical residential purchase in BC, the buyer's agent commission is paid through the seller's side of the transaction. I go over exactly how it works in your case before we start, in writing, so there are no surprises.

q4.resposta: Yes. I work in English and Portuguese, and the whole process, including documents and contracts, can be explained in either language.

q5.pergunta: Do you only work with Brazilian clients?
q5.resposta: No. I work with buyers and sellers across Greater Vancouver and the Fraser Valley. Portuguese is an extra, not the service.

q6.pergunta: What if I am not ready to buy yet?
q6.resposta: Then that is what we will find out together, and it is useful information. Knowing which steps come first is worth more than starting to visit properties too early.

ctaFinal.titulo: Let's talk before you make the decision.
ctaFinal.apoio: A short conversation is usually enough to know where you stand and what the next step is. No pressure, no commitment.

paginaComprar.titulo: Buying a home in BC, with the full <ancora>picture</ancora> in front of you.
paginaComprar.intro: Most buyers do not need more listings. They need to know what they can afford, what the property is really worth and what happens at each step.
paginaComprar.b1Texto1: Before we look at anything, we go through your numbers with a mortgage broker and put the pre-approval in writing. Then I explain the agency agreement and the disclosure form, so you know who I work for before you sign anything.
paginaComprar.b1Texto2: From there it is criteria, regions, alerts and showings, and I say what I would not buy as often as I say what I would. When a property holds up, I pull the comparables and we agree on the number before I write the offer, with the subjects that protect you.
paginaComprar.b1Texto3: Once the offer is accepted, the work is the part nobody sees: inspection, strata documents, final financing approval, subject removal, deposit, lawyer or notary, Property Transfer Tax and completion. Eleven stages, and you know which one you are in.
paginaComprar.b3Texto: Selling and buying at the same time is a logistics problem before it is a market problem. Timing, financing and order of operations planned together.
paginaComprar.b4Apoio: Three documents that tell you what the listing photos never will.
paginaComprar.b5Titulo: Buying from abroad or as a newcomer.
paginaComprar.b5Texto: Different system, different rules, same goal. I explain how the process works here and what changes compared to what you knew.

q1.pergunta: How long does it take, from the first conversation to the keys?
q1.resposta: The search is the part that varies, and it depends on your criteria and on what is available in your range. From an accepted offer to completion the timeline is short and it is written into the contract. I show you the real dates of the properties we are looking at, not an average.

q2.pergunta: What is a subject, and can I lose my deposit?
q2.resposta: Subjects are the conditions written into your offer: financing, inspection, strata documents. While they are in place, the contract is not firm. Once they are removed, it is, and the deposit is committed. That is why nobody removes a subject on my watch before the reason for it is answered.

q3.pergunta: What happens if the inspection finds something?
q3.resposta: That is exactly what the subject period is for. Depending on what it is, we renegotiate, we ask for the repair, or we walk. Finding a problem before the deadline is the inspection working, not the deal failing.

q4.pergunta: Can I buy in BC if I am not a permanent resident?
q4.resposta: The rules on this have changed more than once in recent years, and they apply differently depending on your status, the property and where it is. I check your specific case against what is in force before you spend money on anything, and I put it in writing.

q5.pergunta: Do I have to use a mortgage broker?
q5.resposta: No, and you can go straight to your bank. I suggest talking to a broker because seeing more than one lender usually changes the number you are working with, and that number decides everything after it.

paginaVender.b2Texto: Comparables, property history, current inventory and how long similar homes are taking to sell. Never a number pulled out of the air.

e3.texto: The property is seen on a phone long before it is seen in person.

e4.texto: Showings without offers are information, and the information is usually about the price.

e5.texto: Dates, subjects, deposit and what stays in the house move a deal as much as the number does.

q1.pergunta: How long will it take to sell?
q1.resposta: It depends on the price band, the type of property and the preparation. I show you how long comparable properties actually took in your area, and we plan against those, not against a market average.

q2.pergunta: What do I pay to sell?
q2.resposta: The commission is agreed with you in writing before anything goes live, and it is never a surprise at the end. On top of that come the lawyer or notary and, if there is a mortgage, the discharge. I go through all of it before you decide.

q3.resposta: Usually not. What pays for itself is smaller than people expect: cleaning, light, small repairs and taking things out. I tell you which ones come back in the price and which ones do not.

q4.pergunta: Can I sell and buy at the same time?
q4.resposta: Yes, and it is a logistics problem before it is a market problem. The order of the dates, the financing and what happens if one side moves are decided together, at the start.

q5.pergunta: What if it does not sell?
q5.resposta: We look at price, presentation and timing, in that order, and I tell you which one it is. Sometimes the honest answer is to take it off the market and come back, and I will say that too.

paginaSobre.p1: My career was built on sales, negotiation, market analysis and relationships. Real estate was the natural next step, and it never became about selling a property.
paginaSobre.p2: I have helped more than 100 families with their real estate needs: first-time buyers, families moving into more space, sellers, and clients looking at presales and residential investment.

s2.titulo: Three things in the guide that most people find out too late
s2.b1Texto: The first-time buyer exemption wipes out Property Transfer Tax up to $500,000 and is worth $8,000 up to $835,000. Between $835,000 and $860,000 it phases out. Above that, nothing. The guide lays out the five personal conditions and the property condition that all have to be met at once, and meeting all but one is common.
s2.b2Texto: Since March 2026 there is a federal GST rebate for first-time buyers of new homes worth up to $50,000. It is recent, plenty of people still do not know it exists, and the guide covers who qualifies, what counts as a first-time buyer under this specific rule, and the difference between the builder crediting it at closing and claiming it from the CRA yourself.
s2.b3Texto: Selling before you have owned for 730 days can trigger the BC home flipping tax, and the principal residence exemption does not protect you from it. It reaches people who lived in their own home. The clock includes presale contract dates, it started before 2025, and the return is separate with a 90-day deadline. The guide walks through the four situations where it catches people who are not speculators at all.
s2.simulacao: And the two full calculations. In the buyer example, a $780,000 condo in Surrey needs $11,250 in cash beyond the down payment in closing week. In the seller example, the lines that are not commission come to nearly $12,000, and the biggest one is not the lawyer or the move. It is the mortgage penalty.

s3.linha: REALTOR® with Stonehaus Realty, working across Greater Vancouver and the Fraser Valley. Serving clients in English and Portuguese.
s3.corpo: I work with two kinds of client: people buying for the first time who do not want to get it wrong, and people who already own and are making a move where both ends have to line up. In both cases the first thing I do is the same. I sit down and build the full number, before we look at a single property. This guide is that conversation, in writing.
s3.p1: The guide arrives by email and you read it on your own time. There is no sales sequence dressed up as content.
s3.p2: If you want the version with your own numbers, reply to the email or send COST by direct message. It is four short questions.
s3.p3: I build your calculation and send it over. From there you decide whether to talk strategy or just keep the numbers. Both answers are fine.
